text:
A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect today, so the lake is no place for a casual outing. Burlington is mostly cloudy and sitting at 64, and so far this has been more nuisance than washout. A shower or rumble of thunder can still pop up through late afternoon, but rainfall should stay scattered and light. Winds on the broad lake are running 15 to 25 knots before turning west, with waves 1 to 3 feet, so I’d stay close to shore and be off the water before the wind shift. The shower chance lingers into this evening, mainly before 10, then skies break with a low around 44.

Friday turns cooler and remains unsettled, though the high is uncertain, with forecasts ranging from 54 to 61. I’d bet on the forecasters’ upper 50s, with some sun and another chance of showers. Plan outdoor time today for now, but skip a long lake outing and carry a rain jacket.

week.blurb: Showers may interrupt Thursday, but breaks of sun keep the day mild near 64; carry a light jacket.
Friday looks cooler, with a high near 57 and a shower chance; the models disagree on how warm it'll get.
Sunny Saturday stays pleasantly dry, with a high near 58 and a light southwest breeze.
Sunday turns mostly cloudy but warm near 69, with showers becoming possible after dark.
Monday stays mostly cloudy near 67, with showers possible early and again after dark.
Tuesday is the wet, windy one, with likely showers, a high near 59, and gusts reaching 30 mph.
Wednesday turns cooler and breezy near 51, with early showers possible before a partly sunny afternoon.
